title: Conditional κ = 7.42785663120535e-4: gen5 — compile-cost-annealed pair and all-but-one modules on #276's gen4 bit word, five-stage completed banks
body:
**κ = 148557132624107/(2·10¹⁷) = 7.42785663120535e-4**, conditional, with the bit supplier binding.

| compared with | κ | gain |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| highest open claim when I wrote this (#284, 07:10 UTC Oct 10) | 7.26291692225845e-4 | **+2.27%** |
| #276's gen4 package, which this extends | 7.22869827347495e-4 | +2.76% |

This is a second structural change to the bit word. The gain does not come from frame or entrance tuning.
#276's gen4 word keeps its arc-aware local circuit. Its two **module circuits** are replaced by modules
annealed against the exact one-instance **compile cost**:

| Module | gen4 | gen5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pair + copied centre | 448 additions, debt 184 | 463 additions, 299 arcs, debt 164 |
| all-but-one | 34 additions, debt 12 | 32 additions, 21 arcs, debt 11 |

The virtual word needs 17,292 auxiliary roles: 612 fewer than gen4 and 1,616 fewer than PR200. The
generator is byte-identical to #276's; only its module data and frozen arcs change.

```sh
cd research/five-stage-gen5-banks
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt     # sympy==1.14.0
python3 -B verify.py --output /tmp/gen5-five-stage-verification     # about 5 minutes, no network
```

## What changed

There is one new self-contained package, `research/five-stage-gen5-banks/`, plus its own path-filtered
workflow. No existing file changes. The package is #276's package with the bit word swapped and the
constants re-pinned.

| one invocation, m = 120 | gen4 (#276) | **gen5 (this PR)** |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| virtual auxiliary roles | 17,904 | **17,292** |
| compensated reuse pairs | 1,494 | 1,406 |
| independent dirty registers R | 16,410 | **15,886** |
| independent entrances | 2,466 (ranks 20, 21) | 2,554 (ranks 17, 18, 20, 21) |
| literal stock (60 replicas) | 1,283,035 | 1,247,070 |
| normalized stock / deficit | 256,607 / 52,800 | 249,414 / 52,800 |
| bit coarse saving | 7.23392746398452e-4 | **7.43337804075788e-4** |
| κ | 7.22869827347495e-4 | **7.42785663120535e-4** |

The complex supplier is unchanged (PR234/PR193, coarse 7.47454944651775e-4). The bit side still binds, now
**0.55%** below it, so the complex supplier, for example #233's word (7.547e-4 in this layout per #256),
is about to become the lever.

## Why compile cost and not debt

Minimizing additions − carrier arcs alone is the wrong objective. A cyclic-interval all-but-one module
reaches the proven floor of debt 10, yet costs the whole word 4.5%, because it cuts roles into many
small rank steps.

So both modules were annealed on the exact one-instance compile cost: a single module instance compiled
in its real geometry with the generator's own compiler. Closed-form node-rank evaluators reproduce that
compile up to a constant offset, which allowed long annealing runs (10⁷ or more iterations each).

| Region | Debt change | Raw a_b change (whole word) |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| pair module | 184 → 164 per instance | +1.13% |
| all-but-one | 12 → 11 | +0.83% |
| together | | +2.76% |

The predicted and actual gains agree to 0.01%. `gen5bit/README.md` has the details.

The rank-17 entrances need width-7 bank blocks, so 10 mixed (7¹² 4⁹) banks are used per stage, as
source527 used mixed 11/4 banks. The total residual width is even, so the 60-replica tiling is exact.

## What `verify.py` checks (9 mandatory stages, same as #276)

- **virtual:** the PR168-v4 checker on the virtual word, with all 5 controls rejected; then PR200's
  physical-word proof (1,710 changed frames, 1,406 handoffs, the physical row, the physical word on all
  19,406 columns over F₂ and the integer decoder), with 4 adverse controls rejected.
- **raw / bit:** the census of every physical path (both reflections), the event emitter, parity fusion
  (1,500,000 even payload ADDs elided), the five-stage global lowering (479,144 paid calls, deficit
  4,400), and exact h=24/m=120 geometry, including one actual entrance basis of each rank 17, 18, 20
  and 21.
- **scalar:** the retained source527 scalar program on all 19,406 F₂ columns and the signed integer
  decoder in both directions, with 11 actual-context corruptions rejected. The controls now always pick
  odd-coefficient responses, since even ones vanish over F₂.
- **primes:** 25,802 consumed bases, at most 118 bits, every residual below 2⁸⁰.
- **banks:** 411 exact charts and all 4,765,800 assignments; the 2,554 rank-5a completions are removed.
- **complex, math, finite:** both moment engines with the full 10⁻¹⁶ fallback, all 47 strict
  inequalities and 7 margins (the adjacent κ grid point is rejected), and the literal finite bill with
  757,938,545,400 selector calls.

`gen5bit/producer/regenerate.py` rebuilds the five pinned bit-word files byte for byte, in about 2
minutes. I replayed the package in my working environment, in a clean Python 3.12 + sympy 1.14.0 venv
from another directory, and from a fresh git checkout. All three give the identical certificate.

Outside the package, a read-only audit:

- reproduced the coarse value and κ with its own 400-bit ball arithmetic;
- re-derived every frame, all 1,406 aliases, every target chronology, the F₂ replay on all 19,406 columns
  and the helper ledger with exact arithmetic;
- confirmed that no check was weakened relative to #276.

## Status

This is a conditional finite construction with exactly the retained interfaces of #276, #210 and #234.
There is no new Lean and no multiplier benchmark. The composable gen4 mechanisms (#279–#283: response
kernels, retimings, target-prefix squares, early restorations) should carry over to gen5 with the
constants re-pinned. I have not done that here.
